relevance_reason: The paper tests a known kyphomelic dysplasia variant (KIF5B p.Thr195Lys) in zebrafish and re-reviews the 4 previously published KIF5B-related kyphomelic dysplasia patients. It also reports 3 new dominant KIF5B variants that cause other phenotypes without kyphomelic dysplasia, which shows the KIF5B phenotypic spectrum and heterogeneity.

findings.statement: Flex et al. (2023) injected human KIF5B mRNA carrying the kyphomelic dysplasia-associated p.Thr195Lys (c.584C>A) missense variant into 1-cell zebrafish embryos. By 2 dpf, these embryos had a significant increase in mild and severe heart defects and heart edema. They also had a wider ceratohyal cartilage angle than embryos injected with wildtype KIF5B. Expressing the variant in motoneurons significantly reduced mitochondrial coverage along the axon and caused mitochondrial transport defects. The authors suggested that the variants act as dominant-negative alleles.
quotes: Overexpression of KIF5BThr195Lys and KIF5BAsn255del resulted in a wide range of morphological defects in heart size and anatomy, which were scored as mild or severe, and embryos expressing these variants presented heart oedemas at 2 dpf
the ceratohyal cartilage angle was less acute in all of the embryos injected with mutant KIF5B variants compared to those expressing the WT protein or non-injected embryos

For all injected variants, a similar trend could be observed in particular for p.Thr195Lys and p.Leu498Pro alleles where we measured a significant reduction in the mitochondrial coverage along the axon.

findings.statement: Flex et al. (2023) re-reviewed the 4 previously reported patients with KIF5B-related kyphomelic dysplasia, who carried de novo p.Thr195Lys, p.Gly234Val, or p.Lys91Arg variants. All 4 had neonatal distress and respiratory failure, and their hypotonia partially resolved with age. Single individuals had tracheomalacia, glossoptosis, or velopharyngeal insufficiency. Clubfoot was present in 3 of the 4 patients.
quotes: In particular, the four subjects affected with KD invariably presented with neonatal distress and respiratory failure requiring medical intervention in most cases. Tracheomalacia, glossoptosis and velopharyngeal insufficiency were also present in single individuals. In these subjects, the hypotonia seemed to partially resolve with age.

findings.statement: Flex et al. (2023) noted that the kyphomelic dysplasia-associated KIF5B variants affect residues Lys91, Thr195, and Gly234. These residues lie in the motor domain and cluster in the pocket that binds ATP/ADP. Joint contractures were seen only in patients with motor-domain variants, which suggested a correlation between altered motor-domain function and joint contractures or clubfoot.
quotes: three recently reported missense variants implicated in KIF5B-related KD affected residues (Lys91, Thr195 and Gly234) also mapping at the motor domain, clustering in the pocket mediating ATP/ADP binding

Notably, joint contractures were observed only in subjects carrying pathogenic variants within the kinesin motor domain (p.Asn255del, family 2 of the present series; p.Lys91Arg, p.Thr195Lys and p.Gly234Val, from Itai's series).

findings.statement: Flex et al. (2023) identified 3 other dominantly acting KIF5B variants located further 3-prime than the kyphomelic dysplasia variants: p.Asn255del at the end of the motor domain, and p.Leu498Pro and p.Leu537Pro in the coiled-coil domain. These caused phenotypes ranging from a syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder to adult-onset dilated cardiomyopathy with ophthalmoplegia and skeletal myopathy, without kyphomelic dysplasia apart from scoliosis in 1 patient. The authors proposed grouping these conditions as KIF5B-related diseases.
quotes: Here, we describe three additional heterozygous variants in KIF5B located at the more 3′ end of the gene in the terminal portion of the kinesin motor domain and in the coiled coil domain resulting in a clinically wide phenotypic spectrum
we excluded occurrence of skeletal signs suggestive of KD in our patients (e.g. bent long bones, narrow thorax, and scoliosis) with the exception of scoliosis for subject 1
Based on the wide spectrum of presentation of this heterogeneous group of phenotypes, we propose to group them as KIF5B-related diseases.

findings.statement: Flex et al. (2023) described an Italian boy (subject 1), last evaluated at 8 years 3 months. He had a neurodevelopmental disorder with severe developmental delay and intellectual disability, early-onset refractory epilepsy, and severe hypotonia, and needed a gastrostomy for feeding. He also had progressive cortical atrophy, a thin corpus callosum, and dysmorphic features including bitemporal narrowing, hypertelorism, ptosis, and a short deep philtrum. Severe scoliosis was reported at 9 years.
quotes: Subject 1 (p.Leu537Pro), a 9-year-old male, showed a NDD characterized by severe DD/ID, early-onset refractory epilepsy, hypotonia, feeding difficulties requiring percutaneous gastrostomy, brain abnormalities (i.e. progressive cortical atrophy and thin corpus callosum)
Severe scoliosis was reported at 9 years.

findings.statement: Flex et al. (2023) used trio whole-exome sequencing in subject 1 and identified a de novo heterozygous c.1610T>C (p.Leu537Pro) variant in KIF5B. The variant was absent from gnomAD and affects a conserved leucine in the coiled-coil dimerization region. Fibroblasts from the patient showed abnormal cilia, enlarged and peripherally located lysosomes, and Golgi disorganization. Motoneurons derived from the patient's iPSCs had reduced mitochondrial coverage in the distal parts of their neurites.
quotes: a de novo missense change (c.1610 T > C, p.Leu537Pro) in KIF5B emerged as an excellent candidate
A statistically significant reduction in mitochondrial coverage in the distal part of neurites in motoneurons expressing KIF5BLeu537Pro was observed (Fig. 9C).

findings.statement: Flex et al. (2023) described a family (family 2) with autosomal dominant, adult-onset dilated cardiomyopathy that required heart transplantation in 3 members. Affected members also had skeletal myopathy that worsened over time, ophthalmoplegia, elevated CPK, joint contractures, and peripheral neuropathy. A heterozygous in-frame deletion in KIF5B, c.765_767delCAA (p.Asn255del), segregated with the disorder; it was inherited from the father of a 67-year-old man (subject 2) and was carried by his 2 affected sisters. Zebrafish embryos injected with this variant developed heart defects.
quotes: Subject 2, a 67-year-old male, and his two affected sisters (p.Asn255del) belonged to a family segregating an autosomal dominant form of adult-onset dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) requiring heart transplant in three members

findings.statement: Flex et al. (2023) described a 6-year-old girl (subject 3) with mild developmental delay, severe hypotonia that began prenatally, feeding difficulties requiring G-tube feeding, and mild dysmorphism. She carried a de novo heterozygous KIF5B variant, c.1493T>C (p.Leu498Pro), in the coiled-coil domain.
quotes: Subject 3 (p.Leu498Pro) was a 6-year-old female with mild DD, severe hypotonia, swallowing and feeding difficulties since infancy requiring G-tube feeding for the first 7 months of life, and recurrent vomiting.

relevance_reason: This paper first describes de novo heterozygous KIF5B variants in 4 people with kyphomelic dysplasia. That disorder is the subject of this entry.

findings.statement: Itai et al. (2022) described 4 individuals with kyphomelic dysplasia. All 4 had sharp angulation of the femora and humeri, distinctive facial features, and neonatal respiratory distress. Three had short stature and 3 developed postnatal osteoporosis followed by fractures. Two had brachycephaly and 2 were diagnosed with optic atrophy.
quotes: All individuals had sharp angulation of the femora and humeri, distinctive facial features, and neonatal respiratory distress. Short stature was observed in three individuals.
Three developed postnatal osteoporosis with subsequent fractures, two showed brachycephaly, and two were diagnosed with optic atrophy.

findings.statement: In 2 of 4 individuals with kyphomelic dysplasia, Itai et al. (2022) used whole-exome sequencing to find a de novo heterozygous c.272A>G variant in the KIF5B gene, which results in a lys91-to-arg (K91R) substitution. The affected amino acid is conserved and lies in or close to the ATPase activity-related motifs of the catalytic motor domain.
quotes: All individuals had de novo heterozygous variants in KIF5B encoding kinesin-1 heavy chain: two with c.272A>G:p.(Lys91Arg)
All variants involved conserved amino acids in or close to the ATPase activity-related motifs in the catalytic motor domain of the KIF5B protein.

findings.statement: In 1 individual with kyphomelic dysplasia, Itai et al. (2022) used whole-exome sequencing to find a de novo heterozygous c.584C>A variant in the KIF5B gene, which results in a thr195-to-lys (T195K) substitution. The affected amino acid is conserved and lies in or near the ATPase-related motifs of the motor domain.
quotes: one with c.584C>A:p.(Thr195Lys)
All variants involved conserved amino acids in or close to the ATPase activity-related motifs in the catalytic motor domain of the KIF5B protein.

findings.statement: In 1 individual with kyphomelic dysplasia, Itai et al. (2022) used whole-exome sequencing to find a de novo heterozygous c.701G>T variant in the KIF5B gene, which results in a gly234-to-val (G234V) substitution. The affected amino acid is conserved and lies in or near the ATPase-related motifs of the motor domain.
quotes: the other with c.701G>T:p.(Gly234Val)
All variants involved conserved amino acids in or close to the ATPase activity-related motifs in the catalytic motor domain of the KIF5B protein.

findings.statement: Itai et al. (2022) described kyphomelic dysplasia as a heterogeneous group of skeletal dysplasias with severe bowing of the limbs and other variable features, such as a narrow thorax and abnormal facies. They suggested that heterozygous deleterious KIF5B variants cause a specific form of kyphomelic dysplasia, which extends the phenotypic spectrum of the kinesinopathies.
quotes: Kyphomelic dysplasia is a heterogeneous group of skeletal dysplasias characterized by severe bowing of the limbs associated with other variable findings, such as narrow thorax and abnormal facies.
Our findings suggest that heterozygous KIF5B deleterious variants cause a specific form of kyphomelic dysplasia.
